title: Freeman on reading and not reading jazz books
summary: Freeman says he rarely reads jazz books because he lived the history, but reads a paperback a day.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Life philosophy: faith, karma and how to live

blocks.x: Which no one has ever written about and talked about. It's very easy to dislike a man who's made it, not that you -- you and I are not speaking of that sort of thing, nor am I saying anything original, especially to you, Helen, you know much more about any of these personalities than I because I have been all over the place. I rarely read jazz books with all due respect to the people who have written them, because I was there.

If I am going to spend time reading, I have so much I want to read -- I went over to the Isle of Man not too long ago, to do a couple of shows, radio shows and I did a couple of concerts and I was there about ten days and I read a book a day. I am a great one on paperbacks because they are easy to get and you don't have to lug them around, and when you are finished with them, you just give them to somebody.
And I just love to read, so if I am going to spend all that time reading, I am not going to read about something I have already lived.
I suppose I am an omnivorous sort of reader --
People who like to read are.
Anyway, to get back and finish off with Benny --
